status_note.text: Sold by the Marine Institute to Qikiqtaaluk Corporation in October 2023 and renamed Moses Appaqaq. A 2025–26 dry-dock refit in St. John's, Newfoundland (new Kongsberg-designed gondola and new sonars) was reported in September 2026, followed by an inaugural hydrographic survey off Labrador; first full Arctic season planned for 2027. The refit year is not yet confirmed by the operator, so it is not used as the Rebuilt year.

status_note.text: Active (November 2026). NOAA Ocean Exploration's status page says the ship is in port in Honolulu, Hawai‘i, after the 2026 Technology Demonstration (EX2701, 2–16 November 2026), which tested a HUGIN 6000 and two Orpheus AUVs off Hawai‘i. The 2026 season began after a dry dock in Ketchikan, Alaska. The ship is not laid up and has no announced decommissioning date. NOAA plans to replace it with the new NOAA Ship Discoverer, which NOAA expects to come online in 2028 (delivery June 2028, commissioning late 2029). NOAA says Okeanos Explorer's retirement date will depend on the ship's condition when Discoverer comes online. In March 2026 NOAA said it plans to move ROV operations toward a commercial contract.

timeline.event: Keel laid as USNS Capable (T-AGOS-16) at Halter Marine
Launched and christened at Halter Marine, Moss Point, Mississippi
Delivered to the Navy; in service with Military Sealift Command as an ocean surveillance ship
Struck from the Naval Register and transferred to NOAA (NOAA gives 10 Sept; NavSource gives 14 Sept)
Converted for ocean exploration: ROV hangar, bow and stern thrusters, sonar fairing, new bridge (Todd Pacific Shipyards; Fairhaven Shipyard)
Commissioned as NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer (R 337); named through a student contest won by Woodstock High School, Illinois
First expedition: EX0801 mapping shakedown off Washington
Multibeam upgraded from EM 302 to EM 304
Dry dock in Ketchikan, Alaska, then the 2026 season in the Pacific (Hawai‘i, Cook Islands, American Samoa)
2026 Technology Demonstration (EX2701) with AUVs; now in port in Honolulu

status_note.text: Draft record, compiled from public sources only and not verified with the operator. Unknown values are omitted. Named only as the launch vessel for University of Delaware glider ud_orris on 13 Aug 2026 ('aboard Tips Up out of Lewes, DE') in the mission's ERDDAP metadata. Owner, operator, official homeport, length and identifiers are not stated. A VIMS glider mission the same day also reports a launch 'aboard Tips Up out of Indian River Inlet, DE' with Matt Oliver aboard; that does not by itself establish University of Delaware ownership. The Lewes homeport in the directory is the reported departure, not a confirmed hailing port. Not listed on the CEOE Marine Operations fleet page (accessed 2026-11-25).

lars.text: GMSO lists “U-frame; A-frame; side boom” plus electromechanical hydraulic, trawling hydraulic, oceanographic and auxiliary davit electric winches, and a tender. It says the ship is suited to “USV deployment, repair and recovery”.

notes: GMSO’s page does not name a specific USV, give a safe working load, or give deck space, so those fields are empty rather than guessed.

The page lists R/V Bellows as a GMSO partner vessel, 21.5 m. This registry record MV-0139 (21.5 m) names Florida Institute of Oceanography as operator. The match is by name and length only; confirm it is the same hull and who operates it today.
